title: §12-003: Strategy Pattern & Pluggable Middleware Pipelines
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §12-003 (Strategy Pattern & Pluggable Middleware Pipelines).

cards.concept: Strategy Pattern & Pluggable Middleware Pipelines: EventEmitter Synchronous Execution Semantics
cards.question: In what order and execution model does Node's `EventEmitter` invoke registered listener functions upon `emit()`?

options.text: Asynchronously in the next libuv poll phase via threadpool.
Synchronously, in the exact order in which listeners were registered.
Concurrently on worker threads.
In reverse order of registration.

cards.explanation: EventEmitter invokes all listeners synchronously in registration order. An unhandled error thrown inside one listener prevents subsequent listeners from executing.
cards.pitfall: Emitting an 'error' event on an EventEmitter with no registered 'error' listener causes Node.js to throw an unhandled exception and crash the process.
cards.citation: Node.js Events API Documentation: Passing arguments and this to listeners

cards.concept: Strategy Pattern & Pluggable Middleware Pipelines: EventEmitter Memory Leak Warning
cards.question: What causes Node.js to log `MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected`, and how should it be managed?

options.text: The process has exceeded 2GB V8 heap allocation.
More than 10 listeners (default threshold) have been added to a single event on an emitter, typically indicating unremoved event listeners.
Network sockets are closing prematurely.
The event loop has stopped polling.

cards.explanation: By default, EventEmitter warns if >10 listeners are added to an event. If intentional, tune with emitter.setMaxListeners(n). If unintentional, remove listeners with emitter.off().
cards.pitfall: Adding event listeners inside repeated HTTP request handlers without removing them upon response completion steadily leaks memory.
